title: speculative-decoding-and-model-integration-draft-3
content:
Status: Draft (working notes)
Authors: Aisha Patel (lead), Marco Hernandez, Liam O'Connor
Context / Motivation:
- We want to ship speculative decoding (SD) as a first-class optimization in the serving runtime to improve p95 latency and user perceived throughput for interactive workloads. SD must interact correctly with kernel selection, scheduling, and the KV cache, and must be integrated into our model acceptance/rollback workflows so we can deploy safely across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Goals:
1) Define the runtime behaviour for speculative decoding and how it composes with: kernel selection, scheduling/packing, and KV cache reuse.
2) Specify model integration requirements: acceptance tests, metrics to monitor, and automated rollback triggers.
3) Provide an initial rollout plan (canary -> gradual -> full) and a short list of telemetry/alerts.

Non-goals:
- Fully finalized kernel implementation details (this doc sketches integration points, kernels team to supply low-level APIs).
- End-to-end perf numbers (we will add after benchmark pass).

1) High-level design
- Speculative decoding: spawn a lightweight fast-model (spec model) to predict next tokens concurrently while the main model (target model) computes full next-token logits. We merge speculative predictions into responses when confidence criteria are met to reduce tail latency.
- Two modes: optimistic (early accept if spec_confidence >= threshold) and conservative (spec output used only for prefix caching and internal scheduling, final output always from target).

2) Integration points
A. Kernel selection
- Kernels can expose a fast-path for small-batch, short-seq speculative runs (e.g., int8 1-token lookahead with reduced KV compression).
- API contract (kernel -> runtime):
  - kernel.capabilities: {speculative_fastpath: true/false, max_lookahead, preferred_batch_shape}
  - runtime will prefer kernels that advertise speculative_fastpath when speculative decoding is enabled for a model.
- Kernel teams must guarantee that speculative_fastpath outputs are bit-compatible with canonical path for the same input (modulo expected approximation). If not bit-compatible, the spec confidence calibration must be stricter.

B. Scheduler / packing
- Scheduler must be aware of speculative tasks as lower-latency high-priority sub-tasks.
- Speculative tasks should be scheduled with a target start_time = now + spec_lead (configurable, default 0ms), and have a time_budget (default 10ms) after which they can be preempted by higher priority tasks.
- Packing heuristic: pack speculative runs into small micro-batches (size <= spec_max_batch, default 8) and prefer co-locating spec tasks of the same model and token position to enable KV reuse.
- Fairness: do not let speculative work starve normal decoding; cap speculative CPU/GPU concurrency per worker (configurable per-pool).

C. KV cache interactions
- KV cache semantics must support speculative branches: speculative runs will read from the same KV stream as the main request and may produce temporary KV entries (spec_kv) that are only promoted when a speculative token is accepted.
- Implementation approach:
  - Create ephemeral KV layers for speculative executions (layer id = request_id/speculative/<seq>) stored in ephemeral memory.
  - Promotion: when a speculative token is accepted, merge ephemeral KV entries into the canonical request KV at the corresponding positions.
  - Rollback: if speculative token is rejected, discard ephemeral KV entries.
- Eviction policy: ephemeral KV layers have short TTL (default 2s) and are garbage-collected if not promoted. For long-running streaming sessions, provide bump APIs to extend TTL.

3) Acceptance criteria for model integration (onboarding a model with speculative decoding enabled)
- Functional: SD must not change deterministic outputs for canonical mode when speculative is disabled.
- Perf: measurables vs baseline (same model without SD) on a representative workload:
  - p50 latency <= baseline p50 * 0.95 (target)
  - p95 latency decreased by >= 10% (target)
  - token throughput increased by >= 5% under representative concurrency (target)
- Quality: for speculative token acceptance, measure token-level accuracy against target model logits: spec_acceptance_accuracy >= 98% at configured confidence threshold (default 0.98). Define metric = percent of speculative-accepted tokens that match final target model top-1.
- Safety: aborted speculative runs must not leak into persisted KV or downstream logs.

4) Rollback strategy (automated + manual)
- Automated rollback triggers (per deployment group):
  - Increase in error rate: 5xx rate increase > 0.5% absolute within 10 minutes.
  - Quality regressions: spec_acceptance_accuracy drops below 95% or human-eval regression > configured limit.
  - Latency regression: p95 increases > 10% vs pre-deploy baseline.
- Rollback mechanics:
  - Canary cohorts: enable speculative decoding only for 1% of traffic for 1 hour, monitor metrics. If automated triggers fire, immediately disable SD for the canary cohort and alert on-call.
  - Graceful disable: runtime supports toggling speculative feature flag per model at runtime; when disabled, ephemeral KVs must be drained/GCed and no speculative tasks scheduled for new requests.
  - Hot rollback: route traffic away from instances with SD enabled using routing policies; if necessary, redeploy previous model binary without SD.

5) Metrics & dashboards
- Core metrics (per-model and global):
  - sd_speculative_runs_total (counter)
  - sd_speculative_accepts_total (counter)
  - sd_speculative_rejects_total (counter)
  - sd_accept_rate = accepts / (accepts + rejects)
  - sd_accept_accuracy (percent of accepted tokens that match target top-1)
  - sd_mean_latency_reduction_ms (compared to baseline)
  - sd_p50/p95_latency_with_sd, sd_p50/p95_latency_without_sd
  - sd_ephemeral_kv_memory_bytes (gauge)
  - sd_evictions_total (counter)
- Alerts (examples):
  - sd_accept_accuracy < 95% for 5m -> P1 investigate (possible kernel/model mismatch).
  - sd_ephemeral_kv_memory_bytes > pool_threshold -> P2 reclaim/GC or throttle speculative tasks.
  - sd_p95_latency_with_sd > baseline_p95 * 1.10 for 10m -> P1 rollback.
- Dashboard: per-model tiles with canary cohort breakdown, token-level acceptance confusion matrix, time series of accept_rate and accept_accuracy.

6) Rollout plan
- Phase 0: internal alpha. Run SD on internal traffic only, compare against baseline using offline traces.
- Phase 1: canary 1% traffic (24-48h). Monitor automated triggers and collect human evals on sampled queries.
- Phase 2: ramp to 10% (48h) if stable.
- Phase 3: gradual ramp by doubling every 24h to 100% with manual checkpoints and performance sweep.
- Always ensure fallback path (disable SD per-model or per-route) is <2 minutes to enact.

7) Testing and evaluation harness
- Offline trace runner: replay production traces against spec and target model to compute accept_rate, accept_accuracy, and perf delta.
- A/B live runner: split traffic and collect metrics above plus sampled human evals (via small internal annotation pool).
- Kernel regression tests: ensure kernel fastpath returns comparable logits within numerical tolerance; include 1k fuzz tests.

8) Security / privacy notes
- Ephemeral KV entries must respect redaction/policy logic; treat ephemeral layers as equally sensitive as canonical KV.
- Do not persist speculative-only internal logs to long-term storage unless redacted/anonymized.

9) Open questions / TODOs
- Calibration strategy: how to pick per-model confidence thresholds automatically? (TODO: propose ML-driven calibration job).
- Multi-model speculative pipelines (spec model and target model architecture mismatch): how to best compute confidence when token distributions differ?
- Memory budgeting for ephemeral KVs in constrained Dedicated/Private deployments - propose per-pool configurable caps.
- Kernel API: finalize capability flags and fastpath ABI with kernel team (action: @Marco).

Appendix: quick checklist for onboarding a model with SD enabled
- [ ] Kernel capability check (speculative_fastpath)
- [ ] Offline trace pass: perf + quality
- [ ] Canary config + alert thresholds in place
- [ ] Dashboard and sampled human eval active
- [ ] Rollback/playbook tested in staging
